entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Strength score increases by 1, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

entries.name: Adventuring Age
entries: Between 18–40 years of age. Men and women of Gondor often take up arms or wander the marches in their youth, returning to city or farm when duty to house and realm calls them home.

entries.name: Blood of Númenor
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill History} skill (or {@skill Old Lore|TLotRR} if your table prefers Middle-earth skills for lore of the past).

entries.name: Guardians of the West
entries: You have proficiency with the {@item longsword|PHB} and {@item spear|PHB}.

entries.name: Pipe-Weed Lore
entries: You have proficiency with {@item pipe|TLotRR|pipes}.

entries.name: Starting Virtue
entries: You gain one cultural virtue of your choice from the Men of Gondor list, or a common virtue (see {@book Chapter 4|TLotRR|3|Virtues}).

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write {@language Westron|TLotRR} and {@language Adûnaic|TLotRR}, the ancient tongue of Númenor still preserved among the Dúnedain of the South.

entries.name: Standard of Living: Prosperous
entries: Though war presses upon the borders, Gondor remains a realm of stone cities, well-kept roads, and proud houses. Those who adventure often come from soldiery or lesser noble blood—still better provisioned than many folk of the North.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: Players choosing a background receive a brief personal history, two skill proficiencies, a tool proficiency and two distinctive features:

items: {@background Tower Guard|TLotRR}
{@background Keeper of Lore|TLotRR}
{@background Watcher on the Border|TLotRR}
{@background Far-Reaching Herald|TLotRR}
{@background Protector of the Land|TLotRR}
{@background Counsellor|TLotRR}

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Strength score increases by 1, and your Dexterity score increases by 1.

entries.name: Adventuring Age
entries: Between 16–35 years of age. The Riders ride young and hard; many see their first skirmish before they are twenty, and few who love the open grass wait long to answer the call of the Mark.

entries.name: Horse-Lords
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Animal Handling} skill. When you make a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check related to horses or riding, you may treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10.

entries.name: Spears of the Mark
entries: You have proficiency with the {@item spear|PHB}, {@item shortbow|PHB}, and {@item longsword|PHB}.

entries.name: Pipe-Weed Lore
entries: You have proficiency with {@item pipe|TLotRR|pipes}.

entries.name: Swift on the Grass
entries: Your walking speed is 35 feet.

entries.name: Starting Virtue
entries: You gain one cultural virtue of your choice from the Riders of Rohan list, or a common virtue (see {@book Chapter 4|TLotRR|3|Virtues}).

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write {@language Westron|TLotRR}. Many Riders also know the old songs and names of the Mark in their own tongue, though it is seldom written.

entries.name: Standard of Living: Common
entries: The people of Rohan are hardy and free. Wealth is measured more in horses and honour than in gold; a Rider on the road is well-mounted but seldom overburdened with coin.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: Players choosing a background receive a brief personal history, two skill proficiencies, a tool proficiency and two distinctive features:

items: {@background On Patrol|TLotRR}
{@background A Patient Hunter|TLotRR}
{@background Protector of the Land|TLotRR}
{@background Watcher on the Border|TLotRR}
{@background Restless Farmer|TLotRR}
{@background Far Trader|TLotRR}

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Strength score increases by 2.

entries.name: Adventuring Age
entries: Between 18–45 years of age. Beornings come late to trust and early to anger; those who leave the Vales of Anduin often do so as scouts, guardians of fords, or hunters of Orcs.

entries.name: Mighty Frame
entries: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

entries.name: Unnerving Presence
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Intimidation} skill.

entries.name: Vigilant Sleeper
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened, and magic cannot put you to sleep.

entries.name: Pipe-Weed Lore
entries: You have proficiency with {@item pipe|TLotRR|pipes}.

entries.name: Starting Virtue
entries: You gain one cultural virtue of your choice from the Beorning list, or a common virtue (see {@book Chapter 4|TLotRR|3|Virtues}).

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write {@language Westron|TLotRR}. Many Beornings know the speech of beasts in part, though this is a matter of virtue and lore, not a free language.

entries.name: Standard of Living: Frugal
entries: Beornings keep simple halls and free ranges. Adventurers among them travel with what they can carry and what the wild provides.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: Players choosing a background receive a brief personal history, two skill proficiencies, a tool proficiency and two distinctive features:

items: {@background Forest-Dweller|TLotRR}
{@background Hunter of Orcs|TLotRR}
{@background A Patient Hunter|TLotRR}
{@background Protector of the Land|TLotRR}
{@background Bitter Exile|TLotRR}
{@background Watcher on the Border|TLotRR}

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Dexterity score increases by 1, and one other ability score of your choice increases by 1.

entries.name: Shadow of the Forest
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill. In addition, you can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.

entries.name: Wood-Elf Weapons
entries: You have proficiency with the {@item shortbow|PHB}, {@item longbow|PHB}, and {@item spear|PHB}.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Dexterity score increases by 1, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

entries.name: Tree-Walkers of the Golden Wood
entries: You are at home high in the boughs of the great mellyrn. You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, and you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks made to balance on narrow surfaces or tree branches.

entries.name: Galadhrim Weapons
entries: You have proficiency with the {@item shortbow|PHB}, {@item longbow|PHB}, and {@item shortsword|PHB}.
{@i "For the fashion of Minas Tirith was such that it was built on seven levels…"}

The Men of Gondor are heirs of Númenor in the South—wardens of a long defeat and a stubborn hope. From Minas Tirith, Dol Amroth, and the fiefs of the coast and the White Mountains, they keep the memory of the West while Orcs multiply and the Shadow lengthens in Mordor.
Those who adventure may be soldiers of the Citadel, scouts of Ithilien, scholars of the Houses of Healing, or younger children of noble houses seeking renown before the storm breaks.
{@i "Where now the horse and the rider? Where is the horn that was blowing?"}

The Riders of Rohan—the Eorlingas—dwell upon the wide grasslands of the Riddermark. They love horses as kin, honour above ease, and open sky above stone walls. Their songs remember Eorl the Young and the gift of Calenardhon; their spears remember every raid from the East and every oath to Gondor.
A Rider who leaves the Mark may ride as messenger, éored-scout, or exile seeking a name worthy of the mead-hall.
{@i "He is a skin-changer. He changes his skin: sometimes he is a huge black bear, sometimes he is a great strong black-haired man…"}

The Beornings are the folk of Beorn and his kindred in the Vales of Anduin—stern, solitary, and terrible when roused. They hate Orcs and Wargs, keep the fords and passes, and ask little of the world save to be left in peace. Some among them share Beorn's gift of skin-changing; others are simply mighty men of the mountains and woods.
A Beorning abroad is often a guardian, a tracker of enemies, or a reluctant ally drawn into larger wars.

feat.name: Tower-Guard's Resolve
entries: Long watches on the walls of Gondor have steeled your body and mind.

items: Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this trait, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Heirs of the Sea-Kings
entries: The dignity of Númenor still runs in your house.

items: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

feat.name: Stern Perception
entries: Your eyes are accustomed to piercing deceit and falsehood.

items: Increase your Wisdom or Intelligence by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency in {@skill Insight} or {@skill Perception}. In addition, you have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to perceive lies and deceit.

feat.name: Armour of the Citadel
entries: You fight with the discipline of the guards of the White Tree.

items: Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
While wearing medium or heavy armour, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from non-magical weapons is reduced by 2.

feat.name: Proud and Bold
entries: The renown of your ancestors emboldens your heart in battle.

items: Increase your Strength or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage roll.

feat.name: Horn of the South
entries: Your battle-cry echoes like the ancient silver trumpets of the Tower of Ecthelion.

items: Increase your Charisma or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.

As a bonus action, you can shout a rallying command to one friendly creature within 30 feet who can hear you. That creature gains advantage on the next attack roll or ability check it makes before the start of your next turn. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses upon completing a long rest.

feat.name: Ride to Ruin
entries: When the horns sound, your courage rises with the charge.

items: Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you take the Dash action, opportunity attacks against you and your mount are made with disadvantage until the start of your next turn.

feat.name: Horse-Sense
entries: You and your mount understand one another as kin.

items: Increase your Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You can calm a frightened or startled beast as an action with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check. In addition, any mount you ride has its walking speed increased by 10 feet.

feat.name: Fierce as Fire
entries: The wrath of the Eorlingas burns fiercely in your blood.

items: Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When wielding a spear or sword with two hands, or when attacking while mounted, you deal additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus on hit.

feat.name: Steadfast in the Saddle
entries: You ride with seamless balance and instinctive grace.

items: Increase your Dexterity or Strength by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You have advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to avoid falling off your mount or being knocked prone. In addition, mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed.

feat.name: Songs of the Mark
entries: The heroic lays of Eorl the Young and Helm Hammerhand ring out in your voice.

items: Increase your Charisma or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You gain proficiency in {@skill Performance} (or {@skill Old Lore|TLotRR}). When you and your companions complete a short rest where you sing of ancient deeds, each companion regains 1 additional expended Hit Die (up to their maximum).

feat.name: Nomad of the Riddermark
entries: You know the wide plains, rivers, and hill-folds of the Mark intimately.

items: Increase your Constitution or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.

You gain proficiency in {@skill Survival} (or {@skill Travel|TLotRR}). In addition, moving through non-magical difficult terrain costs you and your mount no extra movement when traversing plains, grassland, or hills.

feat.name: Spider-Bane
entries: You have hunted the children of Ungoliant in the dark wood.

items: Increase your Dexterity or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against poison.

feat.name: Feast of the Woodland Realm
entries: Song and starlight still answer you, even far from the halls of the king.

items: Increase your Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient, you instead gain expertise (double proficiency bonus) with Performance checks.

feat.name: Grace of the Golden Wood
entries: You carry the serene majesty and starlight of the Lady's realm in your heart.

items: Increase your Wisdom or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} or gaining Shadow points from sorcery and despair.
When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

feat.name: Bows of the Galadhrim
entries: The woodcraft of the Galadhrim enables you to move unseen and strike without revealing your presence.

items: Increase your Dexterity or Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill. If you are already proficient, you instead gain expertise (double proficiency bonus) with Stealth checks.
When you make a ranged weapon attack while hidden, missing with the attack does not reveal your position.

feat.name: Skin-Changer's Endurance
entries: Whether or not you share Beorn's full gift, your flesh is hard to lay low.

items: Increase your Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
As a bonus action, you can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier. Once you use this trait, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

feat.name: Wrath of the Vale
entries: When your anger is kindled, few stand before you.

items: Increase your Strength by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Brother to Bears
entries: You understand the ways and speech of four-footed beasts.

items: Increase your Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You can communicate simple ideas with beasts of the wild, especially bears, horses, and hounds. You have advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks to interact with them.

feat.name: Great Stature
entries: Your towering height and broad shoulders grant formidable power.

items: Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Your maximum Hit Points increase by 1 per character level.

feat.name: Night-Sight
entries: Your eyes pierce the shadow and gloom of the mountain vales.

items: Increase your Wisdom or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. Within that range, you can see in dim light as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light.

feat.name: Terrible Voice
entries: Your battle roar mimics the bellow of the great bears of the Misty Mountains.

items: Increase your Strength or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.

As a bonus action, you can let out a terrifying roar. Each enemy within 20 feet of you that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
